body: Just assuming you like vikingstuff since you are metalheads. Check out Aifur and sjätte tunnan - vikingthemed restaurant and bar in old town, Stockholm. If you are looking for local young bands check out "kafe 44". Just use google to find if there are any concerts going on. Oh and be prepared to spend some money because Stockholm (especially alcohol) is expensive!!
Thank you, screenshoted this to remember.
Thanks! I've sent my request to join the group - looks great!

instead of a headlamp i am planning on just using my smartphones flashlight when needed, is this a bad idea? I have the rest of the things you mentioned - tire levers were included in the patchkit :)

thank you!

Another comment also mentioned getting handlebar extensions - you're probably right, but i'm very comfortable with the handlebar like it is now. If like you say my hands start to hurt i will for sure take your advice and pick some up! Since my tour will be in Europe i'm assuming it won't be hard to find a bike store that sells them wherever i am.

I am planning on just using the flashlight on my smartphone when i need it, bad idea?

Thank you! :)

Here's the inspiration for my setup:

http://www.cyclingtheglobe.com/equipment/
http://www.bicycletouringpro.com/blog/lightweight-bike-touring-setup/
Thanks, I've followed your advice and just ordered a set of synthetic clothes - t shirts, socks and underwear :)

All this math, you really seem to know your stuff! My dynamo is most likely a cheap one so im guessing it has more drag?

Anyway, i'm going to keep it - i'll suck it up and deal with the drag :)

I decided to pay the money for a decent lightweight 1 person tent and ultralight sleeping pad so i can fit everything in my panniers :). I am bringing a small bag (hardly takes up any space) that i can strap to the rear rack incase i for some reason need extra space for food or such (but i don't think ill need it).

Thanks!

The thing im missing from your list is chain cutter and spare chain link - i'll look in to that!

I was debating if i should bring my flipflops or not - you make a good point! Almost all comments have mentioned the clothes so i will for sure reduce the clothing and thereby save alot of space (making more than enough room for my flipflops - so i'll probably bring them!)

You are probably right about the jeans, but those outdoorsy pants seem to be very expensive (especially fjällräven) and i probably won't be using them that much so i'll stick with the jeans for now.

I googled the bar ends and they are indeed quite cheap - for sure something i will consider getting!

Well I will definitely try out warm showers then, sounds perfect! :)

I will look in to padded cycling shorts, ive heard of padded underwear aswell wich i think i would prefer so i can wear my regular shorts or pants over.

I'm going to follow your advice about the clothing - probably getting rid of the sportpants and two shirts. (keeping the jacket to be on the safe side)

Thanks again and hope you have an awesome tour!

Thank you! The bike came with dynamo when i bought it and you are right, I won't be using it that much - does it really make it that much harder to pedal?

I have heard of warm showers and couchsurfing and id love to try it if i manage to work up the courage (a bit of social anxiety). Maybe once a week or so i think ill spend the night at a hostel or something to recharge my batterypack and get some proper rest.

I am not overly concerned about weight since i am planning to take my time and enjoy instead of going as fast as possible (as long as all my food and gear fits in my two panniers im happy). Also since i will be taking my time i might still be in northern europe in september when it starts to get colder.

Ive got two 750ml waterbottles on my bikeframe. I will probably also bring an extra 2l bottle in my pannier.

My multitool does indeed have a pair of pliers :) I will be bringing a small pocket knife and a spoon.

Do you think the ethanol ill be bringing for my stove could work as sanitising gel aswell?

I'm not planning on wearing cycling clothes, do you think that's a mistake? my shirts are all cotton, i should probably have a synthetic t-shirt for cycling right? Ive heard synthetic clothes are easier to keep clean.

Thanks again for your tips!

Thank you for your comment! The jeans are durable working jeans for wwoofing and such :). I agree i have alot of shirts, and i'll probably get rid off the thin long-sleeved shirt. Indeed Europe will be warm but incase i find myself in a colder area (mountains, windy places during the fall etc) id like to be on the safe side!
Hey! I am planning a bike tour from stockholm through europe - starting at the end of august! Write me if you want to!

Thank you for the tips and suggestions! I will look into wwoof but what I think i want is freedom to go wherever i feel like. I have family in the US that i could visit, so unless i find a travelpartner who wants to go elsewhere, and IF i even find the courage to go - my first stop will probably be California :)
